free.question: Is WavezFM free?
free.answer: Yes. You can create an account, join rooms, chat, vote and play music for free. Optional subscription features expand personalization and support the platform.

media.question: Which music services are supported?
media.answer: Rooms currently play YouTube and SoundCloud links with timing synchronized across participants.

guests.question: Can I preview a room without an account?
guests.answer: Yes. Guest mode lets you follow public rooms and see what is happening. An account is required to chat, vote or join the DJ queue.

rooms.question: Can I create and moderate my own room?
rooms.answer: Yes. Rooms have configurable staff, permissions, a DJ queue, bots, events, polls and moderation tools.

customization.question: What can be personalized?
customization.answer: Profiles can use avatars, badges, backgrounds and frames. Rooms can also configure their theme, colors, room background, welcome message and banner.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Policy explains how WavezFM collects, uses, shares, stores, and protects personal data when you use the platform, including rooms, chat, playlists, profiles, payments, and connected services.

paragraphs.p1: This Privacy Policy applies to WavezFM websites, applications, authenticated areas, live rooms, and related services. By using the Service, you acknowledge the practices described here.
paragraphs.p2: This Policy should be read together with the Terms of Service and Cookie Policy. If a feature provides a more specific privacy notice, that notice also applies to the feature.

paragraphs.p1: WavezFM is responsible for deciding why and how personal data is processed in connection with the Service. Privacy requests may be sent to hi@wavez.fm.
We process information you provide when creating and using an account or communicating through the Service.

items.i1: Account data, such as email address, username, display name, password hash, and authentication or two-factor details.
items.i2: Profile data, such as avatar, biography, country flag, badges, social connections, preferences, and public profile settings.
items.i3: Content and communications, including room chat, whispers, reactions, polls, giveaways, reports, support requests, uploaded media, room settings, and bot configurations.
items.i4: Music and community activity, including playlists, imported tracks, room participation, DJ queue activity, votes, favorites, follows, and moderation actions.
items.i5: Transaction details, such as purchases, subscriptions, gifts, donations, currency, amount, provider, and payment status. Full card details are handled by the payment provider, not stored by WavezFM.

paragraphs.p1: When you access the Service, we may automatically record technical and usage information required to operate, secure, and improve it.

items.i1: IP address, browser, operating system, device type, language, time zone, screen information, and approximate location inferred from IP.
items.i2: Session identifiers, cookies, local storage, authentication state, security signals, and connection or WebSocket diagnostics.
items.i3: Pages and features used, clicks, errors, performance information, room presence, playback events, and timestamps.
items.i4: Security, moderation, and audit logs used to prevent abuse, investigate incidents, and enforce platform or room rules.

paragraphs.p1: If you connect or use an external service, we may receive the information needed to provide that integration.

items.i1: Discord may provide an account identifier, username, avatar, and authorization information when used for login or account linking.
items.i2: Last.fm may provide account and authorization information used for scrobbling when you enable the integration.
items.i3: YouTube, SoundCloud, Spotify, Google Drive, and other media services may provide links, identifiers, metadata, artwork, availability, and playlist information.
items.i4: Stripe and Mercado Pago provide transaction identifiers, payment status, billing cycle, currency, amount, and limited billing information required for support, accounting, and fraud prevention.

paragraphs.p1: We use personal data for the following purposes:

items.i1: Create, authenticate, secure, recover, and maintain accounts.
items.i2: Operate rooms, synchronized playback, chat, whispers, playlists, profiles, social features, bots, polls, giveaways, and notifications.
items.i3: Process purchases, subscriptions, gifts, virtual balances, and donations and provide transaction support.
items.i4: Personalize language, appearance, accessibility, privacy, content, and notification preferences.
items.i5: Moderate content, enforce rules, investigate reports, prevent fraud, spam, abuse, and unauthorized access, and protect users and the Service.
items.i6: Diagnose failures, measure performance, develop features, and produce aggregated or de-identified statistics.
items.i7: Meet legal, regulatory, accounting, tax, and dispute-resolution obligations and respond to lawful requests.

paragraphs.p1: Depending on the context and applicable law, processing may rely on one or more of the following bases:

items.i1: Performance of a contract, when data is necessary to create an account or provide a requested feature.
items.i2: Legitimate interests, including service security, abuse prevention, product improvement, and community moderation, balanced against your rights.
items.i3: Consent, when required for optional cookies, certain integrations, marketing, or other optional processing; consent may be withdrawn.
items.i4: Compliance with legal or regulatory obligations, including financial records and valid authority requests.
items.i5: Protection of rights, safety, and legal claims, where permitted by law.

paragraphs.p1: WavezFM does not sell personal data. We disclose only what is reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy.

items.i1: Service providers that support hosting, storage, content delivery, email, authentication, anti-abuse controls, media integrations, and payment processing.
items.i2: Room staff and platform staff when needed for moderation, support, safety, audit, or incident investigation.
items.i3: Authorities, courts, or other parties when required by law or reasonably necessary to protect rights, safety, users, or the Service.
items.i4: A successor organization in a merger, restructuring, financing, or transfer of the Service, subject to appropriate confidentiality and notice requirements.

paragraphs.p1: Usernames, display names, avatars, badges, public biographies, room activity, chat messages, reactions, playlist or room information, and other content you choose to publish may be visible to other users according to your settings and the feature used.
paragraphs.p2: Do not publish personal or confidential information that you do not want others to see. Room privacy and profile controls reduce visibility but cannot prevent another person from recording or sharing content they can access.

paragraphs.p1: We keep personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary to provide the Service, maintain security and moderation records, resolve disputes, and meet legal, tax, accounting, or regulatory duties. Retention varies by data type, room configuration, account status, and legal requirement.
paragraphs.p2: After account deletion, data may remain for a limited period in backups, fraud-prevention records, transaction records, or logs that must be preserved. Public content may be deleted, anonymized, or retained when necessary to preserve conversation integrity, enforce rights, or comply with law.

paragraphs.p1: We use reasonable technical and organizational safeguards appropriate to the nature of the data. No online service can guarantee absolute security.

items.i1: Encrypted transport for supported connections and secure password hashing.
items.i2: Authentication, access controls, permission checks, and two-factor options.
items.i3: Logging, rate limits, abuse detection, backups, and incident investigation procedures.
items.i4: Restricted administrative access based on operational need.

paragraphs.p1: Depending on where you live, including under the LGPD or GDPR, you may have the following rights. We may request information necessary to verify identity and protect the account before fulfilling a request.

items.i1: Confirmation that personal data is processed and access to that data.
items.i2: Correction of incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated data.
items.i3: Deletion, anonymization, or blocking where legally applicable.
items.i4: Restriction of processing or objection to certain processing.
items.i5: Portability of data in an applicable machine-readable format.
items.i6: Information about entities with which data was shared.
items.i7: Withdrawal of consent without affecting prior lawful processing.
items.i8: Review of decisions based solely on automated processing, when applicable.
items.i9: A complaint to the ANPD, an EU supervisory authority, or another competent local authority.

paragraphs.p1: WavezFM and its providers may process data in countries other than your own. Where required, we use recognized safeguards such as contractual protections, adequacy decisions, security measures, and data-minimization practices.

We use essential technologies for authentication, security, session continuity, language, and core operation. Optional preference technologies are used according to your choices where consent is required.
paragraphs.p2: You can manage supported choices through the cookie controls and your browser. Disabling essential storage may prevent authenticated or security-sensitive features from working. See the Cookie Policy for more details.

paragraphs.p1: The Service is not directed to anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their personal data. If you believe a person under the applicable minimum age provided data to WavezFM, contact hi@wavez.fm so we can investigate and take appropriate action.

We may update this Policy as the Service, providers, or legal requirements change. Material changes may be announced on the site, in the application, or by email. The date above identifies the current version.
To ask a privacy question or exercise a data right, email hi@wavez.fm with enough information to identify your account and request. Do not send passwords or full payment-card details.
paragraphs.p2: You may also contact the competent data protection or consumer authority in your jurisdiction, including Brazil's ANPD or the supervisory authority in your EU or EEA country, where applicable.

paragraphs.p1: WavezFM uses YouTube API Services to retrieve public video metadata and availability information. YouTube videos play through an embedded YouTube player.
paragraphs.p2: WavezFM stores video links, IDs, and metadata in playlists and room activity records. The embedded YouTube player may receive browser, device, and network data and use cookies under Google's Privacy Policy.

paragraphs.p1: WavezFM is a place to listen to music together in live rooms. People take turns as DJ, discover tracks, chat, collect items, and build communities around the music they love.

join-room.question: How do I find and join a room?

paragraphs.p1: Open Explore, search or browse the available rooms, then select one to join. Each room has its own hosts, rules, music style, and queue settings. Check the room description and welcome message before jumping in.

guest-access.question: Can I try WavezFM without an account?

paragraphs.p1: Guest previews are available when enabled by WavezFM. Create an account and sign in to participate fully, save playlists, use your profile, and keep your progression. Some rooms or actions may have additional access requirements.

become-dj.question: How do I become the DJ?

paragraphs.p1: Add playable tracks to a playlist and make it your active playlist. In a room, join the DJ queue. When your turn arrives, the room plays from your active playlist. Hosts can lock the queue, require a role, apply cooldowns, or limit track duration, so check the room rules if you cannot join.

woot-meh-grab.question: What do Woot, Meh, and Grab do?

paragraphs.p1: Woot is a positive vote for the current track; Meh is a negative vote. Grab lets you save a track to a playlist so you can find or play it later. Votes, room rules, and staff actions can affect playback. Saving a track does not download its audio or video.

cinema-display.question: How do Cinema mode and the player display controls work?

paragraphs.p1: When available for the active media, use Enter cinema mode on the player for a larger viewing layout and Exit cinema mode to return. Hide video / Show video changes the desktop video display; hiding the video is separate from muting the audio or using Turn player off. The controls available depend on your device and the current media.
paragraphs.p2: Open Settings → Appearance for stage, audience, and SFW display preferences. Use the player volume and mute controls to manage your audio.

playback-trouble.question: Why is a track silent, unavailable, or not starting?

paragraphs.p1: First check your player volume and mute settings. Your browser may require a click before playing audio. A track can also be deleted, region restricted, age restricted, or unavailable for embedding. Try another track, reconnect if your connection dropped, and contact room staff if the issue affects everyone.

earn-xp.question: How do I earn XP and level up?

paragraphs.p1: Eligible Woot votes, DJ plays, and live-room participation when room-wide rewards are enabled can award XP. Your total XP determines your level. Awards follow cooldowns, playback eligibility, daily limits, and any active bonuses; every click or track does not necessarily earn XP.
paragraphs.p2: Sending more chat messages or adding tracks to playlists does not automatically award XP. Open Progression to see your level, milestones, and achievements.

missing-xp.question: Why did I not receive XP for an action?

paragraphs.p1: You may still be on a reward cooldown, have reached a daily allowance, or have played a track that did not meet the minimum duration or listening requirements. A normal DJ play also needs another active listener and a Woot. Repeating the same track too soon can also prevent a reward. Bonus events and account boosts can change eligible rewards.

daily-xp-allowance.question: How does the daily XP allowance reset?

paragraphs.p1: When enabled, the daily XP allowance limits eligible activity rewards and resets at the start of each new UTC day. Its size and the reward cooldowns are configured by WavezFM. The allowance is consumed by qualifying reward actions, so it is not simply a timer measuring how long you leave a room open.
paragraphs.p2: After you use the allowance, affected actions stop awarding XP until the next UTC day. Eligible base coin rewards may still be awarded, subject to their normal cooldowns and requirements.

claim-rewards.question: How do I earn and receive rewards?

paragraphs.p1: Keep an eye on Progression for level milestones and achievement requirements. Eligible achievements can award currencies, XP, badges, or other items. Some rewards are granted automatically, while some milestones unlock an item for purchase rather than adding it to your inventory. Check the reward description and My Stuff.

coins-diamonds.question: What are coins and diamonds for?

paragraphs.p1: Coins and diamonds are separate currencies used for eligible purchases in the Shop. Each item shows the currency, price, and requirements that apply to it. Earn eligible rewards through progression and achievements, and check the Shop for the available purchase options.

events-giveaways.question: Where can I find events, giveaways, and bonus periods?

paragraphs.p1: Rooms can organize events and giveaways, and WavezFM may run bonus periods. Read the event or giveaway rules for entry requirements, timing, and rewards. When the calendar is enabled, the Events control in a room shows scheduled events. A room bot may also provide its own games and giveaways with separate rules.

set-badges.question: How do I choose the badges shown on my profile?

paragraphs.p1: Open Profile and use the badge picker to select badges you own. You can display up to three selected badges. The selection is saved automatically. My Stuff → Badges shows your collection, while the profile controls choose what you display. The chat badge option controls badge display in chat.

get-badges.question: How do I get new badges?

paragraphs.p1: Badges can come from achievements, the Shop, subscriptions, gifts, or special awards, depending on the badge. Check each badge's description and requirements. Owning or displaying a cosmetic badge does not automatically grant a room staff role.

equip-items.question: How do I change my avatar, background, or other cosmetics?

paragraphs.p1: Open My Stuff to find the items you own and equip supported cosmetics. Browse the Shop to preview available items and their prices or requirements. Profile customization and room appearance are separate: changing room backgrounds or video frames requires the appropriate room permissions.

edit-profile.question: Where do I edit my profile and preferences?

paragraphs.p1: Open Profile for your public identity and selected badges. Open Settings for account, privacy, security, appearance, and available integrations. Public profile information is visible to other users; choose carefully what you share.

missing-item.question: Why can I not use an item I can see in the Shop?

paragraphs.p1: An item may require purchase, a level, an achievement, an active subscription, or another eligibility condition. A catalog preview is not ownership. Check its requirements and your inventory, and contact support if a completed purchase is missing.

playlist-count.question: How many playlists can I have on my account or profile?

paragraphs.p1: There is currently no fixed cap on the number of playlists you can create. The account limit applies to tracks inside each playlist, not the number of playlists. Free accounts and subscribed accounts can have different track limits; the current comparison is shown under Accounts & subscriptions.
paragraphs.p2: Your playlists belong to your account library. The Music tab on your public profile shows recent DJ tracks, not a public list of your saved playlists.

create-playlist.question: How do I create a playlist and add music?

paragraphs.p1: Open Playlists, create a playlist, and use its add or import controls. Search for music or paste a supported media link, then select the tracks you want to keep. Available sources and import options depend on the current platform settings. Review imported tracks before using them in a room.

Your active playlist is the one used for your DJ turns. Choose the playlist you want to play and make it active before joining a queue. Keep playable tracks in it and arrange their order to prepare your set.

supported-music.question: Which music services can I use?

paragraphs.p1: YouTube is a supported playback source, and other sources such as SoundCloud are available when enabled. Importing a Spotify playlist does not mean the Spotify audio plays directly: imported entries must resolve to supported playable media. Availability depends on the source, region, and room rules.

find-track.question: How do I find a song I heard earlier?

paragraphs.p1: Open Recently Played for your listening history, or check the room's playback history. Use Grab while a track is playing to save it to one of your playlists. A deleted or restricted source can become unavailable later.

vanilla-account.question: What does a free account include?

paragraphs.p1: With a free account, you can join available rooms, listen together, chat, take DJ turns when the room permits, build playlists, follow people, customize your profile with eligible items, and earn eligible progression rewards. Room creation and uploads follow the current account limits. Paid catalog items and subscription benefits have their own requirements.

subscription-benefits.question: What additional benefits come with a subscription?

paragraphs.p1: Subscriptions add the benefits currently offered by WavezFM, such as increased account limits and access to eligible premium catalog items. The comparison below uses the current settings. Premium access does not mean every paid item is automatically owned.
paragraphs.p2: Check the Shop and Settings → Subscription for the plan, price, duration, and exact benefits before purchasing. XP bonuses, extra emoji access, and other perks are included only when explicitly enabled and listed.

manage-subscription.question: Where can I check or manage my subscription?

paragraphs.p1: Open Settings → Subscription to see your subscription status, renewal or expiry information, payment history, and the available management controls. Follow the options shown for your plan and payment method. Buying a subscription does not grant room moderation powers.

gift-subscription.question: Can I give someone a subscription?

paragraphs.p1: When gifting is available, use the subscription gift option and confirm the recipient before paying. The recipient and duration are shown during the purchase flow. Supporter or gift badges follow their own eligibility rules and are different from a room staff role.

subscription-expiry.question: What happens when my subscription ends?

paragraphs.p1: Benefits that require an active subscription stop applying when access expires, and free account limits apply again. Check Settings → Subscription for your current status and renewal options. The availability of particular items depends on their requirements; contact support if you need help with a purchase or billing issue.

fans-superfans.question: What are Fans, Following, and Superfans?

paragraphs.p1: Fans are people who follow you. Following lists the people you follow. Superfans are mutual connections: you follow each other. These are social connections, not paid subscription tiers.
Open their profile from chat or the room's People list, then use the follow control. Manage your connections from Fans. If they follow you back, the connection appears among your Superfans.

Communities bring people and rooms together around shared interests. Explore the Communities page to discover them and check the options available for each community. Community membership and room staff permissions are separate.

private-messages.question: How do whispers and private messages work?

paragraphs.p1: Use the available message or whisper control on a user's profile or in the room to start a private conversation. Availability can depend on privacy settings, blocks, and account permissions. You can manage privacy preferences in Settings and report inappropriate behavior.

create-room.question: How do I create and manage a room?

paragraphs.p1: Use the create-room control in Explore, then configure the room name, description, rules, and available settings. Your account has a limit on rooms you own. Room staff can help manage the space according to their role, while some settings remain restricted to the Host or Co-host.

room-roles.question: What do Host, Co-host, Manager, Bouncer, R.DJ, and VIP mean?

paragraphs.p1: Room roles apply within a particular room. The room's owners and authorized staff assign them; a subscription does not automatically make you staff. These are the general roles; each room can customize names and permissions.

items.i1: Host: the room owner, with the highest room authority.
items.i2: Co-host: helps the Host manage the room and its staff.
items.i3: Manager: helps operate and moderate the room within their permissions.
items.i4: Bouncer: helps enforce chat and room rules through moderation tools.
items.i5: R.DJ (Resident DJ): a trusted DJ role that can enter a locked queue by default.
items.i6: VIP: a recognized room member; it is not a general moderation role.
items.i7: User: a regular participant. Specific actions can still be restricted by room settings.

platform-roles.question: Are platform roles different from room roles?

paragraphs.p1: Yes. Admin, Developer, and Ambassador are platform roles, while Host, Manager, and similar roles belong to a room. Subscriber indicates subscription access. Verified and cosmetic or custom roles have their own meaning and do not automatically grant every staff permission. Role names and appearances can be customized.

room-rules.question: Why can another room let me do something this one cannot?

paragraphs.p1: Each room can configure queue access, playback rules, chat behavior, polls, bots, and other features within the platform limits. Room bans, mutes, or temporary queue restrictions may also affect your actions. Read the room rules and ask its staff for clarification.

replies-mentions-reactions.question: How do replies, mentions, and message reactions work?

paragraphs.p1: Open a message's actions and choose Reply to answer with its context attached. Type @ and select a person from the suggestions to mention them. Use Add reaction / React to choose an emoji for a message. Room-wide and role mentions require the appropriate permissions.
paragraphs.p2: Select Mentions in the chat to find messages that mention or reply to you. Configure mention alerts and sounds in Settings → Notifications; browser notifications also depend on your browser permission.

chat-features.question: Can I use GIFs, animated emojis, images, and polls?

paragraphs.p1: Use the chat composer controls to find available emoji, GIF, and upload options. Rooms can have custom emojis and polls when enabled. Upload size, message length, and access depend on account and room settings. Opening a preview lets you inspect shared media; only use links and files you trust.

setup-room-bot.question: How do I set up a bot in my room?

paragraphs.p1: A room bot runs through WavezFM's bot API using a room-specific token. You need permission to manage bots in that room. Creating a token alone does not start or host a bot.

items.i1: Open the room's management settings and go to Bots.
items.i2: Create a bot token with a name, prefix, required permissions, and lifetime. Copy the secret token when it is shown; it is displayed only once.
items.i3: Configure your bot application or supported bot service with the room and token, following its setup guide.
items.i4: Start the bot, connect it to the room, and test its commands and permissions.
items.i5: Keep the token private. Revoke or rotate it if it is exposed or no longer needed.

bot-commands.question: Why is a bot command not working?

paragraphs.p1: Commands are provided by the bot running in that room. Check that it is online, that the command name and prefix are correct, and that your role and the bot's token allow the action. A muted bot, a revoked token, or disabled room settings can block a command. Ask the room's bot manager for its command list.

bot-features.question: What can a room bot do?

paragraphs.p1: Depending on its implementation and granted permissions, a bot can respond in chat, read room events, assist with queue and playback, moderate, and run games or automations. Bot permissions are explicit and room scoped. Developers can use the HTTP API, realtime events, and the WavezFM JavaScript/TypeScript SDK.

account-integrations.question: Where can I connect other services?

paragraphs.p1: Open Settings to see the integrations currently available for your account. Features such as Discord connections or Last.fm depend on platform availability and your authorization. Review the connection status there, and disconnect a service when you no longer want to use it.

Join the official WavezFM Discord or use the support email below. For room-specific rules, queues, or moderation questions, start with that room's staff. Include the room, approximate time, and a clear description when reporting a technical issue; never send your password or bot token.

report-user.question: How do I report a user or message?

paragraphs.p1: Use the report action available on the user or message, choose an appropriate reason, and provide useful context. Reports go to the relevant moderation workflow. Blocking or muting someone is different from filing a report, and room staff can address immediate room issues.

help-sos.question: What is the room's help / SOS control for?

paragraphs.p1: Use the room's help or SOS option to request moderation assistance when it is available. Explain the ongoing problem clearly so the team can review it. General feature questions and billing issues are better directed to the support channels below.

account-security.question: How can I keep my account secure?

paragraphs.p1: Use a unique password, verify your email, and enable two-factor authentication in Settings when available. Review connected services and do not share sign-in codes, recovery codes, or bot tokens. Use the password recovery flow if you lose access.

rules-privacy.question: Where can I read the platform rules and privacy information?

paragraphs.p1: Read the Terms, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy for platform-wide information. Rooms also publish their own rules, which apply alongside the platform terms.
